recipes.name: Garlic Pasta
ingredients_raw: 1 medium head garlic, peeled and chopped

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add penne and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, 8 to 10 minutes.

While the pasta is cooking, add oil and garlic to a large skillet over low heat. Cook until oil is hot and garlic is sizzling, 8 to 12 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in parsley, basil, oregano, and pepper flakes.
Drain pasta and transfer to a large bowl. Add oil and garlic mixture, toss to coat, and let sit for 3 to 5 minutes. Sprinkle with Parmesan and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Garlic Pasta
raw_recipe.description: Garlic pasta made with a whole head of garlic is for ideal for allium lovers! Parmesan cheese, chopped fresh herbs, and red pepper flakes add to this dish.

review.reviewBody: This is a classic Italian side dish with much room for improvisation and versatility. Add more or less garlic to suit your tastes, but I would strongly advise against sauteing it for 10-15 minutes as the recipe directs. Browning the garlic is a risk that should definitely be avoided as it turns unpleasantly bitter. Just saute it for about 30 seconds to a minute, depending on the heat you're using, until fragrant. I also reduced the crushed red pepper significantly--it's presence should be subtle. Use herbs alone or in combination--no need to measure, just add to suit your taste. As with any cooked pasta, reserve some of the cooking water to add to the pasta if necessary as it sits.

Delicious! I make pasta with garlic & oil all the time, and this is so very versatile. I do add some butter to the garlic and oil mixture, about 3 tablespoons. I also heat the mix over low heat for about 15 minutes, do not brown the garlic, just let it heat and steep in the oil. You could easily adjust the pepper and herbs to taste, this is such a wonderful, yet delicious dish that never seems to fail. Sometimes I like to add some steamed broccoli at the last minute, which is wonderful also. Thanks for sharing :)

This easy recipe did not disappoint. We have 2 meat eaters, a vegetarian and 2 vegans in our house. This was a great meal that accommodated all of us. I added: 1/2 chopped onion, one chopped green pepper, one chopped red pepper and 2 Cups sliced mushrooms to the pasta mixture. Then I grilled some chicken and put it and the cheese on the side. Everybody loved it. The 8 serving recipe fed 5 of us well - no left overs. Next time I will cut the suggested amount of crushed red peppers in half.
Simple. Easy to make. Mixed chopped onions with the garlic. Next time, I will try to add a little bit (2 TB?) of white wine.

Not super great, but good and very easy. Used bowtie pasta, used dried herbs - 1tsp for every TBL. Added 3 T butter to the oil to cook garlic in. DO NOT brown garlic, but sautee for a few minutes. Reduce red pepper to less than 1/2 tsp or omit alltogether. Add 2 c steamed broccoli.

I added shrimp to the garlic, oil and seasonings in skillet. Let garlic sauté for only 1-2 mins on med. I added the seasoning pinch by pinch to my liking and salt. Went light on red pepper. Used shaved Parmesan cheese on top.

This recipe will be added to my list of regular sides. I added some peas and tomatoes for color and to add a serving of veggies to the meal. I also chopped fresh parsley and dried basil because I didn't fresh basil. Yummy!

It was good, but I found that it had quite a lot of bite to it. I don't know if it was all the garlic or spices. Also I think another type of pasta would be better. With penne all the spices get clogged in the inside of the pasta.

I also added about one 8 oz bag of tyson grilled chicken to the garlic and seasoning mix while I was cooking it to make it a little bit of a more heartier main dish.

I have read a few reviews, and have noticed that quite a few people have said that the amount of herbage was simply overwhelming. And I can't help but wonder if they used dried herbs, rather than fresh.
I used fresh herbs in the amounts recomended, and found myself eating a very fresh, very beautiful bowl of pasta. I did serve mine with additional grated parmesan on the side, and found that everyone used more, so perhaps the cheese could have been doubled. Given that the cheese is the only source of salt in this recipe, that may be the reason why we used so much extra cheese. Perhaps a sprinkling of salt would have cured that...
Having said all that, I find myself making this often when I have a need for a good flavour, but little time.
Final note: one other adjustment I made was to add a bit of lemon juice. Again, I served wedges at the table, and left each to their own. Some used it, some did not. I have tried it both ways, and it really depends on my mood, and how rich the other dishes I served alongside it. With other rich dishes, the lemon is a must. With light dishes on the side, I found it excessive.

absolutely delicious even though I had to substitute dried basil and oregano for fresh. I'm sure it would have been even better had I had the fresh herbs. I suggest being careful when cooking the garlic, it does so rather quickly and u don't want the taste of burnt garlic to ruin the entire dish. I added baby bella mushrooms(sauteed with garlic) and spinach which I added towards the end just to wilt.

I made this last night and it was delicious! I baked the head of garlic so it wasn't bitter at all. Just add it to oil with the rest of the ingredients, add a little pasta water and you're good to go.
Has virtually no flavour and is very time consuming to make. This recipe is deceiving.
It was a lil spicy but i'll moderate next time the red pepper flakes to less than the recipe calls for. Besides that I love it.
I used vegan grated Parmesan cheese

This was pretty tasty! Almost too tasty. Hard not to go back for more. I love garlic; and even I was a bit overwhelmed. I personally liked the kick the red pepper flakes gave, but if you don't tolerate spice you should definitely consider reducing that too. Overall pretty decent recipe and near perfect!
